A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TSRBench and contain readable text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G. The complete material supports reliable comparison, including renamed tasks and relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations in Table 2, tool-use and inference-time experiments, resolution studies, and error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds three model evaluations, multivariate coverage statistics, and an open-ended forecasting experiment.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction process and deterministic analysis-tool pipeline in Appendices D–E remain unchanged. Additional baseline evaluations and rendering explanations do not introduce a new proposed algorithm or model.

E1.justification: Appendix F.3 adds an open-ended forecasting scenario requiring models to generate future numerical values rather than select a candidate sequence. The underlying benchmark retains 4,125 instances, 14 domains, and 15 task categories; renamed tasks and newly reported multivariate proportions do not establish new datasets.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds TimeOmni-1-7B, OpenTSLM-tsqa-sp-3B, and OpenTSLM-tsqa-flamingo-3B. All previously reported model rows remain. Other newly mentioned models in the setup, including Qwen3-1.7B and Phi4-Multimodal-8B, already appeared in v1's table.

E3.justification: Appendix F.3 introduces direct numerical forecasting evaluated with nMAE and compares its model-size correlations with those from MCQ accuracy. Existing benchmark settings remain stable; the expanded plotting description documents previously unspecified details rather than establishing a changed rendering protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix F.3 adds a benchmark-validity check asking whether MCQ and open-ended forecasting produce similar scaling trends. Existing tool-augmentation, resolution, reasoning-effort, contamination, and error analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The existing Spearman correlation analysis and significance-reporting convention are retained. The added forecasting correlations reuse that approach; no new repeated-run information, seeds, confidence intervals, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: All 41 shared Table 2 rows retain their scores. Added overall accuracies are 36.7% for TimeOmni-1-7B, 31.0% for OpenTSLM-tsqa-sp-3B, and 30.7% for OpenTSLM-tsqa-flamingo-3B. Table 8 adds numerical-forecasting/model-size correlations of -0.61 for LLMs and -0.05 for VLMs; Table 9 newly reports 58.1% multivariate instances overall.

T1.justification: Appendix E's regression, peak-detection, change-point, and lag formulations are unchanged, as are the mathematical examples in Appendix G. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The benchmark contribution and headline findings are retained. The abstract modestly qualifies the claimed gap in prior benchmarks, changing time-series reasoning from being 'notably absent' to a dimension that existing benchmarks 'largely overlook.'

C2.justification: Appendix F.3 newly interprets similar model-size correlations as evidence that MCQ accuracy faithfully reflects open-ended forecasting quality. This adds an interpretation of benchmark validity; the original explanations of scaling behavior, modality complementarity, and error bottlenecks remain.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies line charts, vertically stacked multivariate subplots, shared time axes, enabled gridlines, and series labels. Table 5 adds access links for the three newly evaluated models. The 100-PPI setting and statistical-summary injection were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds four references, including OpenTSLM and MMMU-Pro, while retaining the overall related-work framing and benchmark comparison. It also corrects MMLU/MMMU terminology to match the referenced work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language corrections, standardizes Pattern Recognition and Comparative Analysis terminology, reconciles model descriptions, adds an Impact Statement, and expands Appendix F. The main section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Two appendix tables are added, the former Table 8 becomes Table 10, and Tables 2 and 5 gain model rows. Figure 11 is redrawn with reordered slices and 'Domain-Agnostic' replacing 'Unlabeled,' retaining the percentages. Captions, figure sizing, and appendix case layouts also change.

improvement.justification: The additional baseline evaluations, explicit rendering details, and multivariate breakdown make v2 modestly more complete and reproducible while preserving the existing empirical results. The new forecasting-format check addresses a useful validity question, although its claim of faithful agreement is stronger than similar model-size correlations alone establish. These gains support a limited overall improvement.
